display.title: Episode 399: The Hour of Fortune (Chol HaMoed Sukkos)
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Sukkos show: why Sukkos is the 'time of our joy' for us and for Hashem, and the parable of a servant given one hour to gather the king's treasures.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that Sukkos is called 'zman simchaseinu', a joy shared by the Jewish people and by Hashem: after Yom Kippur our record holds only mitzvos, so nothing blocks Hashem's blessings from reaching us. We fill the days with special mitzvos like the sukkah and the four kinds, share them with others, and build up to Simchas Torah, when we dance with the Torah. 'V'samachta b'chagecha' means it is our own holiday, happening now, in a year the Rebbe called a year of miracles. After the Hakochainik march and the Shema, Uncle Yossi tells 'The Hour of Fortune': a loyal servant named Yisroel is allowed one hour in the king's treasure room to take whatever he likes, but a violinist's beautiful music keeps distracting him until the hour runs out and he leaves with empty barrels. Uncle Yossi explains the parable: the King is Hashem, the treasure room is this world, the treasures are mitzvos, and the musician is the yetzer hara. The show closes with Chag Sameach wishes and a reminder to find out when Hakafos are held in shul.
display.lesson: Our time in this world is a precious hour to gather mitzvos; don't let the yetzer hara distract you until the time is gone.

date.note: 'A happy Chol HaMoed Sukkos to all of you' and 'this new year, Tav-Shin-Nun': Tuesday of Chol HaMoed 5750 is 17 Oct 1989, matching the weekly estimate.
